subtitle: Generals of Devagiri: How Frontier Lords Carried a King’s Wars

panels.shot: epic split-composition wide, two commanders framed against opposite horizons
panels.action: Kholeshvara stands on a dusty northern plain with fort ramparts behind him, while Bichana faces a lush southern hill-fort and distant sea, both in Yadava war attire, separated by a diagonal of marching troops.

dialogue.text: In Singhana II’s age, it was not the king alone who rode to war, but Kholeshvara in Lata and Bichana in the south, turning Devagiri’s frontier lords into a war machine.

i18n.hi: सिंहण द्वितीय के समय, अकेला राजा नहीं, बल्कि लाट का खोलेश्वर और दक्षिण का बिचना भी रण पर चढ़े, देवगिरी की सरहदी रियासतों को युद्ध मशीन बना दिया।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of Devagiri fort and radiating campaign routes
panels.action: The stone bastions of Devagiri rise from a rocky hill; painted lines and streams of tiny cavalry stretch out across a stylised map toward Gujarat in the northwest and Goa, Dharwad and Saundatti in the south.

dialogue.text: Inscribed stones and court poems agree: under Singhana II, Yadava power spread far beyond Devagiri. But how did one hill-fort rule lands from Lata to Goa?

i18n.hi: शिलालेख और दरबारी कविताएँ मानती हैं: सिंहण द्वितीय के अधीन यादव ताकत देवगिरी से कहीं दूर तक फैली। पर एक पहाड़ी किला लाट से गोवा तक कैसे राज चला पाया?

panels.shot: tight overhead on an old copperplate inscription being examined
panels.action: An aged copperplate and a stone inscription lie on a scholar’s desk, their Nagari script sharply lit while the surroundings fade into shadow.

dialogue.text: The answer hides in records like Kholeshvara’s Ambejogai inscription of 1228 CE and in the verses of Kirti-Kaumudi and Hammira-mada-mardana, each telling the story from a different side.

i18n.hi: जवाब छिपा है खोलेश्वर के १२२८ ई. के अम्बेजोगाई शिलालेख में और कीर्ति-कौमुदी व हम्मिर-मद-मर्दन के छंदों में—हर एक अपनी तरफ से कथा कहता है।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Devagiri fort at dawn
panels.action: Devagiri’s cliffside walls glow in the first light of dawn; within, silhouettes of scribes, armourers, and horse-handlers move, hinting at a busy war administration.

dialogue.text: By c. 1215 CE, Singhana II ruled from Devagiri over a rising kingdom. To grow further, he needed more than courage; he needed men who could command in his name, far from his gaze.

i18n.hi: लगभग १२१५ ई. तक सिंहण द्वितीय देवगिरी से उभरते राज्य पर राज कर रहा था। आगे बढ़ने को उसे सिर्फ जिगर नहीं, ऐसे मर्द चाहिए थे जो उसकी नज़र से दूर रहकर भी उसके नाम पर सेनाएँ चलाएँ।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in a royal hall
panels.action: Inside a pillared audience hall, Singhana II is implied off-frame as we see Kholeshvara and Bichana standing before an empty throne, each holding palm-leaf orders and sword-belts, faces composed and resolute.

dialogue.text: Kholeshvara, settled in Khandesh and Vidarbha, and Bichana, rooted in the southern marches, were among those trusted hands. They were feudatory lords, yet also the king’s generals.

i18n.hi: खानदेश–विदर्भ में जम चुके खोलेश्वर और दक्षिणी सरहदों में जमे बिचना, ऐसे ही यक़ीनी हाथ थे। वे सामंत ज़रूर थे, पर साथ ही राजा के सेनापति भी।

panels.shot: split-panel style, close-up on each face with different landscapes behind
panels.action: On one side, Kholeshvara’s calm, weathered face is backed by the dry plateau and river valleys of Khandesh; on the other, Bichana’s keen gaze is framed by forested hills and a distant coastal strip.

dialogue.text: Their lands were not mere gifts. They were fiefs tied to duty: hold the frontier, gather men, ride when Devagiri called, and in return, rule under the Yadava banner.

i18n.hi: उनकी रियासतें सिर्फ इनाम नहीं थीं, फ़र्ज़ से बँधी जागीरें थीं—सरहद थामो, सिपाही जुटाओ, देवगिरी बुलाए तो घोड़े कसो, और बदले में यादव ध्वज तले हुकूमत करो।

panels.shot: dynamic wide of troops assembling in two different mustering grounds
panels.action: Kholeshvara oversees armoured horsemen and archers forming ranks on a dusty field near the Godavari; Bichana inspects mixed contingents from Ratta, Gutta and Kadamba country in a greener camp lined with palm trees.

dialogue.text: Modern historians see here a pattern—like later nayaka systems, but less formal on record. Feudatories mustered their own forces, yet these troops moved as parts of Devagiri’s larger wars.

i18n.hi: आज के इतिहासकार यहाँ एक ढाँचा देखते हैं—बाद के नायक प्रथा जैसा, बस कागज़ पर ढीला। सामंत अपनी फ़ौजें खुद खड़ी करते, पर वही फ़ौजें देवगिरी की बड़ी जंगों में हिस्से बनकर चलतीं।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Kholeshvara riding out, with map inset of Lata coast
panels.action: Kholeshvara rides at the head of a column of cavalry, banners snapping in the wind, as a faint overlay suggests the route north-west toward the rich coastal tract of Lata.

dialogue.text: Kholeshvara’s Ambejogai inscription speaks of a campaign into Lata—the Gujarat littoral. It praises his role, placing him at the heart of Yadava efforts to push toward the western sea.

i18n.hi: खोलेश्वर का अम्बेजोगाई शिलालेख लाट—यानी गुजरात के समुद्री किनारे—पर चढ़ाई की बात करता है। वह उसकी भूमिका गाता है, उसे यादवों के पश्चिमी सागर तक धकेलने की कोशिश का केंद्र दिखाता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of Lata battlefield with opposing standards visible
panels.action: On a coastal plain with distant sea haze, Yadava cavalry faces off against enemy lines marked by Gujarat-style standards, each side tense as war-drums are raised.

dialogue.text: Kirti-Kaumudi, written in western India, sees these conflicts from the other camp, praising Gujarat’s resistance. It counters Yadava claims, reminding us each inscription serves its own king.

i18n.hi: पश्चिम भारत में लिखी कीर्ति-कौमुदी इन्हीं लड़ाइयों को दूसरी तरफ से देखती है, गुजरात की मज़बूती का गुणगान करती है। वह यादव दावों को काटती है, याद दिलाती है कि हर शिलालेख अपने राजा की सेवा करता है।

panels.shot: dramatic mid-shot of Kholeshvara in council tent at night
panels.action: By lamplight in a campaign tent, Kholeshvara studies palm-leaf letters and a rough map of Lata while officers wait for orders, shadows long on the canvas.

dialogue.text: “Our task is clear: break their hold on the coast, hold it for Devagiri.”

i18n.hi: "काम साफ़ है: उनके तटीय पंजे तोड़ो, और किनारा देवगिरी के नाम पर थामो।"

panels.shot: montage wide of sieges and negotiations without graphic violence
panels.action: A sequence shows Yadava troops encamping before walled towns, lines of envoys entering gates, and fortress doors opening, all under a changing sky from morning to dusk.

dialogue.text: The Ambejogai inscription condenses many hard days into praise: captures, submissions, new tribute flows. It names Kholeshvara not as a stray raider, but as a central figure in this western thrust.

i18n.hi: अम्बेजोगाई शिलालेख कई कड़े दिन कुछ पंक्तियों में समेट देता है—क़ब्ज़े, आत्मसमर्पण, नई हूक-कर की धाराएँ। वह खोलेश्वर को छिटपुट लुटेरा नहीं, इस पश्चिमी धावे का धुरी दिखाता है।

panels.shot: ceremonial interior shot of Kholeshvara at Ambejogai temple
panels.action: Kholeshvara stands before a temple at Ambejogai, hands folded, as craftsmen carve an inscription on stone in the background.

dialogue.text: By 1228 CE, at Ambejogai, his achievements were fixed in stone. From Khandesh and Vidarbha, he had carried Singhana’s banner into Lata and returned with new claims of glory.

i18n.hi: १२२८ ई. तक अम्बेजोगाई में उसकी जीतें पत्थर पर जड़ दी गईं। खानदेश और विदर्भ से वह सिंहण का ध्वज लाट तक ले गया और नए यश-दावे लेकर लौटा।

panels.shot: wide shot of southern hill-country with multiple feudatory camps
panels.action: In rolling hills dotted with small forts, Bichana rides along a ridge as contingents bearing Ratta, Gutta and Kadamba symbols move below, their different armour and dress visible.

dialogue.text: While Kholeshvara worked the northern and western lines, Bichana turned south. Sources and modern studies tie his name to the Rattas, Guttas and Kadambas—local powers drawn into Yadava folds.

i18n.hi: जब खोलेश्वर उत्तर–पश्चिम की रेखाएँ साध रहा था, बिचना दक्षिण मुड़ गया। स्रोत और आधुनिक शोध उसे रट्ट, गुण्ट और कदम्बों से जोड़ते हैं—स्थानीय ताकतें जिन्हें यादव घेरे में खींच लिया गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bichana in negotiation within a southern fort hall
panels.action: Inside a stone hall of a southern fort, Bichana sits with a Ratta chief; weapons rest aside as they gesture over palm-leaf agreements and heaps of coins.

dialogue.text: “Keep your lands, your gods, your customs—but ride when Devagiri calls.”

i18n.hi: "जमीन तुम रखो, देवता तुम रखो, रिवाज़ तुम रखो—पर देवगिरी पुकारे तो साथ सवार हो।"

panels.shot: wide coastal shot of Goa region with banners and ships
panels.action: A rugged coastal landscape, suggestive of Goa, shows a Yadava banner flying over a hill-fort while small ships lie anchored below, soldiers moving between shore and stronghold.

dialogue.text: Through such bargains and campaigns, Bichana helped lock down the southern chain—from Dharwad and Saundatti toward Goa—giving Devagiri a reach to the western coast from another direction.

i18n.hi: ऐसी सौदाबाज़ी और मुहिमों से बिचना ने दक्षिणी कड़ी कस दी—धारवाड़–सौंदत्ती से गोवा की तरफ—देवगिरी को पश्चिमी तट तक दूसरा रास्ता दे दिया।

panels.shot: intercut of Hammira-mada-mardana manuscript and marching Yadava troops
panels.action: A manuscript of Hammira-mada-mardana lies open while, in a ghosted overlay, Yadava troops file past with steady discipline, hinting at the reality behind the poetic boasts.

dialogue.text: Hammira-mada-mardana, praising other rulers in Rajasthan, also touches these wars, presenting Yadava advances as threats to be checked. It confirms their reach, even as it celebrates resistance.

i18n.hi: राजस्थान में दूसरे राजाओं का बखान करती हम्मिर-मद-मर्दन भी इन जंगों को छूती है, यादव बढ़त को रोके जाने लायक ख़तरा दिखाती है। वह उनके फैलाव की तस्दीक करती है, भले ही मज़ाहमत का गुणगान करे।

panels.shot: diagrammatic overhead of the Deccan with coloured zones for delegated power
panels.action: A stylised map of the Deccan shows Devagiri at the centre, with coloured stretches marking Kholeshvara’s northern sphere and Bichana’s southern sphere, arrows indicating campaign directions.

dialogue.text: Taken together, inscriptions and texts show a pattern: Singhana II did not ride to every frontier. He relied on men like Kholeshvara and Bichana, whose own bases became springs for wider war.

i18n.hi: मिलाकर देखें तो शिलालेख और ग्रंथ एक नमूना दिखाते हैं: सिंहण द्वितीय हर सरहद पर खुद नहीं चढ़ा। उसने खोलेश्वर और बिचना जैसे मर्दों पर भरोसा किया, जिनकी अपनी रियासतें दूर तक फैली जंग की छलाँग-पट्टी बन गईं।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of both generals in quiet reflection at Devagiri
panels.action: Kholeshvara and Bichana stand side by side on Devagiri’s ramparts at sunset, looking out over distant lands now bound to the hill-fort, their faces thoughtful rather than triumphant.

dialogue.text: “We hold our frontiers—and in doing so, we hold the king’s future.”

i18n.hi: "हम सरहदें थामते हैं—और इसी में राजा का आने वाला कल थाम लेते हैं।"

panels.shot: slow pull-back from the hill-fort into a wider Deccan landscape
panels.action: The viewpoint withdraws from Devagiri until the fort is a small shape amid valleys, rivers and coasts, with faint echoes of armies and markets flowing between regions.

dialogue.text: Their story reminds us: a kingdom’s strength often lies not just in its throne, but in the many trusted hands that carry its wars and bind its frontiers, far beyond the king’s shadow.

i18n.hi: उनकी कहानी याद दिलाती है: राज्य की ताकत सिर्फ तख़्त में नहीं, उन कई भरोसेमंद हाथों में होती है जो उसकी जंगें झेलते हैं और सरहदें बाँधकर रखते हैं—राजा की परछाईं से बहुत दूर।

subtitle_i18n.en: Generals of Devagiri: How Frontier Lords Carried a King’s Wars
subtitle_i18n.hi: देवगिरी के सेनापति: कैसे सीमा-प्रभु ने राजा की लड़ाइयाँ ढोईं
